title: Controls Engineer, AWS Controls Engineering
descriptionHtml:
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.

Key job responsibilities
Train and assist internal customers and stakeholders with the creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning and operation of BMS and EPMS systems.

Provide technical assistance and support to operations during life cycle of the data center. Review results and action items from the quarterly maintenances for BMS and EPMS and take actions to get them resolved.

Develop BMS & EPMS projects scope of work, schedule, budget, and level of efforts (LOE) to projects requested by customers and stakeholders.

Manage scope, schedule, finance and execution of BMS and EPMS improvement projects in AWS data centers.

Assist in procurement related activities including request for quotation/proposals, responding to request for information, review of vendors proposal and issuance of purchase orders.

Participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate BMS and EPMS technical support to in-service data centers.

Attend project related meetings, coordinate with project leaders and regularly report status to Controls and stakeholders’ management.

Support Controls projects related commissioning activities in the data centers.

Review, implement, troubleshoot and iterate on the controls sequence of operation (SOO) and provide necessary feedback to the design team.

Develop and modify controls logic programming and graphical user interfaces.

Manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements and navigate challenging situations.

Financially manage BMS and EPMS service contracts.

Frequently visit (locally) assigned in-operation and/or under construction data centers to troubleshoot, meet customers, supervise vendor’s work to ensure compliance with the scope, design, SOO and applicable local codes.

A day in the life
As a Data Center Controls Engineer, your primary customers are Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO), who depend on you to deliver reliable, well integrated Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring Systems (EPMS). The problems you solve are technical: modifying controls logic to address operational issues, developing Methods of Procedure (MOPs) for firmware upgrades, or investigating complex alarm discrepancies across monitoring systems. For new builds, you own the controls scope from vendor submittal review through commissioning and turnover. You manage vendor relationships, budgets, and schedules for both service contracts and capital projects. Your internal stakeholders include your Controls Manager, Controls Technicians you provide technical direction to, and partner teams (Construction, Critical Projects Implementation, Commissioning, DCEO).

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of industrial controls and automation experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or an equivalent engineering science plus 5+ years of relevant controls experience, OR 10+ years of relevant controls experience in lieu of a degree.
- 4+ years of general contractor and vendor management work (request for proposals, bidding, change orders, quality control, RFI/submittal tracking) associated with construction and project execution experience

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with Industrial control systems, both hardware and software
- Master's degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, material science, physics or equivalent, or MS degree
- Experience designing, configuring, programming, installing, troubleshooting or servicing HVAC Controls or Electrical SCADA systems application specific controllers, software and networks.
- Experiencing using common industrial communication protocols (MQTT, BACnet and/or MODBUS).
- Demonstrated understanding of engineering documentation, electrical and mechanical diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
- Ability to manage multiple stakeholder deliverables, requirements, and navigate difficult situations.

title: Controls Engineer, EMEA Controls
descriptionHtml:
Are you ready to keep the cloud running at a time of rapid growth? Amazon Web Services (AWS) Infrastructure Services is expanding its data center footprint, and we need a Controls Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for maintaining, troubleshooting, and improving the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS) that govern the mechanical and electrical infrastructure of our data centers. You will plan and execute preventive and corrective maintenance, manage improvement projects, and collaborate with operations teams to ensure our facilities run safely and reliably.

This is a compelling time to join: you will have the opportunity to shape controls standards from the ground up while driving improvements across an expanding portfolio. If you are a self-starter who thrives on solving complex technical problems and wants to grow your expertise in mission-critical infrastructure, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Plan, coordinate, and perform preventive and corrective maintenance on BMS and EPMS systems, adjusting work plans based on equipment conditions and risk assessments to maintain safe, reliable data center operations.
- Manage the scope, schedule, and execution of controls improvement projects, including developing the sequence of operations (SOO), modifying controls logic programming, and commissioning new systems during data center builds.
- Troubleshoot complex mechanical and electrical control issues across generators, switchgear, chillers, cooling towers, and related infrastructure, escalating abnormal conditions when necessary and acting as an escalation point during incidents.
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders, design teams, and external vendors to review maintenance outcomes, align on project deliverables, and ensure all work complies with applicable codes and standards.
- Contribute to process improvements and provide hands-on training to less-experienced team members on equipment operation, BMS/EPMS configuration, and technical best practices.

A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing outstanding maintenance actions and aligning priorities with your facility manager. Much of your time is spent on the data center floor — inspecting equipment, validating controls sequences, and working alongside vendors to commission new systems or resolve open issues. Between site visits you collaborate remotely with design and project teams, reviewing drawings, updating logic programming, and reporting progress to stakeholders. As part of a global on-call rotation, you also stay prepared to provide immediate technical support when the unexpected happens.

About the team
Our controls team sits within AWS Infrastructure Services, the organization that designs, builds, and operates all of AWS's global data center infrastructure. We are the people who keep the cloud running — ensuring the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling systems our customers depend on are always available. The team is growing quickly and playing a central role in delivering reliable infrastructure at scale.

You will work alongside engineers, operations managers, and supply chain specialists in an inclusive culture that encourages bold ideas and continuous learning. You will have real impact on the infrastructure that millions of customers rely on every day.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field
- Experience in vendor management
- Experience in a data center or other critical environment
- Experience in data center engineering or operations
- Experience with Microsoft Office including Outlook, Word, and Excel

Preferred qualifications

- Electrical or mechanical Journeyman License
- operating engineering license such as DC II, DC III, or equivalent
- Experience in construction or project management

title: Software Development Engineer III, AWS AI/ML Servers
descriptionHtml:
AWS runs the world's largest fleet of AI/ML accelerator servers. When a model with billions of parameters trains across a large scale of GPUs, the software that provisions, monitors, and heals that fleet is what keeps training on track. We build the services, control planes, and data platforms that turn hundreds of thousands of servers into a reliable, self-managing system. If you want to build software at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems and the physical infrastructure powering frontier AI, this is the role.

We are seeking a Software Development Engineer to design and build the software that operates our accelerated compute fleet: fleet-management services, orchestration and remediation control planes, telemetry and analytics pipelines, and the APIs and tools that engineering, operations, and partner teams depend on. You will own software from design through production, working across multiple teams and organizations to deliver scalable, reliable services.

What You Will Do

You will design and build distributed services and data platforms that manage the fleet end to end. You will turn ambiguous problems into well-architected software: designing APIs, choosing data models, making the latency, availability, and cost trade-offs that come with operating at fleet scale. You will build the control planes that automate provisioning, health evaluation, and remediation, and the pipelines that transform raw telemetry into signals other teams act on. When your service catches and routes a failing node automatically before it disrupts a training job, that is your impact.

Why You Will Love It

Your software runs across a large scale of servers in the cloud, and you see its impact on fleet availability within days of shipping. You solve genuinely hard distributed-systems problems, own services end to end, and work close enough to the hardware to understand exactly what your software is managing. The team is small enough that your design decisions shape the architecture, and large enough that you always have experts to learn from across software, hardware, and operations.

The Ideal Candidate

You are a strong software engineer first: you design clean abstractions, write high-quality, testable code, and reason about correctness, scalability, and failure modes. You care about the customer of your software, whether that is an operations engineer, a partner service, or an internal tool user. You communicate clearly, raise the engineering bar for your team, and can partner with hardware, firmware, and operations engineers to build software that reflects how the fleet actually behaves.

Key job responsibilities
Service & Platform Development

1. Design, build, and operate scalable distributed services and control planes that automate fleet provisioning, health evaluation, and remediation across a large scale of servers
2. Design APIs, data models, and system architectures that balance latency, availability, durability, and cost at fleet scale
3. Own software end to end: design, implementation, testing, deployment, and production operations, following engineering best practices for code review, source control, and CI/CD

Data & Telemetry Platforms

1. Build data and telemetry pipelines that ingest, correlate, and transform signals from across the fleet into actionable insights and automated actions
2. Develop analytics and reporting services, dashboards, and alerting that give engineering and operations teams real-time visibility into fleet health
3. Apply appropriate algorithms and data structures to process high-volume telemetry efficiently and reliably

Reliability & Operational Excellence

1. Instrument services for observability; participate in post-incident reviews, identify contributing causes, and drive permanent software fixes that eliminate whole classes of risk
2. Improve the resilience, performance, and cost of the services you own, and reduce operational load through automation
3. Produce clear, maintainable documentation for services, APIs, and runbooks so others can operate and extend your work

Technical Leadership & Collaboration

1. Decompose complex problems into well-scoped components that you and other engineers can deliver in parallel
2. Partner with systems, firmware, hardware, and operations engineers to translate fleet behavior into software requirements and correct abstractions
3. Review designs and code, mentor engineers, and set engineering standards for the team

May require occasional (<10%) regional and international travel to Design and Manufacturing Partner sites.

A day in the life
You start the day reviewing a design document for a new remediation control-plane API, leaving feedback on the data model and failure handling. Mid-morning, you pair with a teammate to debug elevated latency in the telemetry ingestion service and ship a fix. In the afternoon, you review overnight metrics from a service you own, then write code for a new fleet-health scoring pipeline. You end the day in a design review with a partner team, aligning on the API contract your service will expose to their tooling.

The Hardware Engineering AI/ML UltraServer platform team is a group of engineers and technical program managers directly responsible for launching GPU-accelerated servers into the AWS fleet. Located in Seattle, Austin, and Cupertino, we collaborate with global development teams and ODM partners to deliver next-generation AI/ML infrastructure deployed in datacenters worldwide. We move fast with small, empowered teams delivering end-to-end, from server conception through fleet-scale operations.

- 5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience

title: Data Center Chief Engineer , DCEO
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic Data Center Engineering Operations Team and become a critical architect of the infrastructure that powers global cloud computing. You'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of Amazon Web Services' physical infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that support millions of customers worldwide.

The Data Center Chief Engineer (CE) is responsible for ensuring that all electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating at peak efficiency. This involves both planned preventative maintenance of equipment, daily corrective work, and emergency response to emergent issues. The CE serves as an expert technical resource reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager, interacting with onsite Engineering Operations Technicians (EOT) and any third-party vendors. They are expected to be a singular focal point for all facility operations within a given data center and to support Amazon within its owned and operated data centers. Data center equipment that supports mission-critical servers must maintain better than 99.999% uptime.

Chief Engineer will be responsible for managing small-to-medium large impact projects from conception to completion. These projects can involve large amounts of independent work as well as collaboration with external support groups including engineering, automation, processing, and finance in both local and global settings. The CE will be tasked with creating and delivering milestones, obtaining and tracking quotes for all necessary costs, and documenting project results for future implementation at other facilities. The goals of such projects are for the CE to drive innovation and resiliency while reducing operational costs in the facilities.

The Chief Engineer directs, trains and supports EOT’s in their role of providing hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations. Implementation and execution of site/equipment-specific training exercises is also expected. This equipment includes, but is not limited to, stand-by diesel generators, switchgear, UPS’s, PDU’s, AHU’s, chillers, cooling towers, chemical treatment systems, pumps, motors, VFD’s, and building automation systems.



AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.



Key job responsibilities
Oversee the day-to-day operations and maintenance of mechanical and electrical equipment in a data center.

Operate independently with limited direct management

Act as an escalation point for all facilities-related issues within the data center, escalating to the Data Center Facility Manager as needed

Perform root cause analysis of equipment failures

Troubleshoot and report of facility and data sever-level events within internal SLA

Create and deploy new standard practices for Engineering Operations Technicians, Chief Engineers, and vendor support teams

Provide training and guidance to Engineering Operations Technicians

Ensure all safety procedures are adhered to by vendor and Amazon staff

Ensure all security procedures are adhered to by vendor and Amazon staff

Utilize internal CMMS to manage building workflows

Communicate complex technical information to a non-technical audience

Using Microsoft Office suite (Outlook, Excel, PPT, Word) and other computer programs such as PDF, QUIP, and other dashboards and scheduling tooling.

Instruct others on scheduling, ticketing, and providing mentorship in developing solutions.



Physical Requirements:

Walk job sites in uneven terrain

Work at heights and from ladders

Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 40 pounds or more

Coordinate body movements when using tools or equipment

Reach and stretch to position equipment and fixtures while maintaining balance

Bend or twist the body into unusual positions while working

Perform physical tasks all day without becoming overly tired

Use hands to manipulate small wires and objects

Push or pull heavy objects into position

Work in a noisy environment

Work at depths, such as under raised floors



This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:

Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

title: Sr. Solutions Architect, GFS Solutions Architecture
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for experienced and motivated technologists who possess a unique balance of technical depth and strong interpersonal skills. As a Solutions Architect, you will partner some of the world's largest financial services companies, AWS Sales and several other AWS teams to craft highly scalable, flexible and resilient cloud architectures that address customer business problems and accelerate the adoption of AWS services.

In collaboration with sales, you will drive revenue growth across a small set of systemically important global financial services customers. As a trusted customer advocate, the solutions architect will help these organizations understand best practices around advanced cloud-based solutions, and how to migrate existing workloads to the cloud. You will have the opportunity to help shape and execute a strategy to build mindshare and broad use of AWS within enterprise customers. This role supports accounts with active migration pipelines and growing AI/ML engagement, requiring an SA who can maintain technical continuity across in-flight workloads while positioning AWS's generative AI and machine learning capabilities.

The ideal candidate must be self-motivated with a proven track record in software, technology sales or consulting. The ability to connect technology with measurable business value is critical for a solutions architect. You should also have a demonstrated ability to think strategically about business, products, and technical challenges. The ideal candidate will bring depth in AI/ML and generative AI, with the ability to guide customers through complex migration programs and position AWS as the target platform for modernization at scale.

Here are some other qualities we are looking for:

Be great fun to work with. At AWS, we have a credo of "Work hard. Have fun. Make history". In this role, you will love what you do and instinctively know how to make work fun. You will be dynamic and creative, and willing to take on any challenge and make a big impact.

Enjoy working with large, global customers. You will have a passion for educating, training, designing, and building cloud solutions for a diverse and challenging set of enterprise customers.

The ideal candidate will have worked as a solutions architect within a Financial Services company (preferably) or other regulated industries. They will have demonstrated industry domain and solutions expertise throughout their career. They possess a deep understanding of various software development methodologies, including CI/CD, DevOps, and MLOPS. They should also have hands-on experience with AI/ML workloads, including model deployment, inference optimization, and generative AI solution architecture.

Key job responsibilities
In partnership with the broader account team, develop technical elements of the strategic plan for accelerating adoption of AWS across the customer's lines of business.

Solutions Architects own the overall technical relationship between customers and AWS and make recommendations on security, cost, performance, reliability and operational efficiency.

Educate customers of all sizes on the value proposition of AWS, and participate in deep architectural discussions to ensure solutions are designed for successful deployment in the cloud

Conduct one-to-few and one-to-many training sessions to transfer knowledge to customers considering or already using AWS

Act as a technical liaison between customers, service engineering teams and support

Capture and share best-practice knowledge amongst the AWS solutions architect community

Author or otherwise contribute to AWS customer-facing publications such as blog posts and white-papers

Build deep relationships with senior technical individuals within customers to enable them to be cloud advocates

Architect solutions leveraging AWS technology, including solution development and potentially demonstrate technical feasibility through mechanisms including proof-of-concepts and/or prototype

Travel may be required for this role, up to 25%

A day in the life
Your mornings might start with a stand-up alongside your account team, aligning on what's happening across your customer's engineering groups this week. From there, you could be in a working session with customer architects sketching out how a new ML inference pipeline could run on AWS, or reviewing an RFP response with your sales counterpart.

You'll be the person your customer calls when they need a trusted technical opinion, whether that's evaluating the right approach for modernizing a legacy application or figuring out how to operationalize a generative AI use case. Some weeks you'll be heads-down building; other weeks you'll be presenting architecture options to a room of senior technology leaders.

This role sits at the intersection of financial services domain expertise, hands-on cloud architecture, and AI/ML. Expect to partner closely with AWS specialist teams and service product teams when opportunities call for deeper expertise in areas like security, data analytics, or generative AI.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud.

AWS Sales, Marketing, and Global Services (SMGS)
We're responsible for driving revenue, adoption, and growth from the largest and fastest growing small- and mid-market accounts to enterprise-level customers including public sector. The AWS Global Support team interacts with leading companies and believes that world-class support is critical to customer success. AWS Support also partners with a global list of customers that are building mission-critical applications on top of AWS services.

The AWS Industries Team
We're committed to helping industry customers enable their digital transformation journeys. Our primary goal is to meet customers where they are in their cloud journey and work backwards from their industry specific needs to transform their business and their entire industry. Our team speaks the language of our industry customers, which means that we focus on business outcomes and industry use cases on behalf of our customers, whether that is how we build products and solutions, how we sell, how we deliver, or how we partner.

title: Manager I Ops, NOC Relay Ops
descriptionHtml:
Looking for a career at a company that seeks to be Earth’s most customer-centric company? If so, meet Amazon.

Over the past 20 years, Amazon has reinvented on behalf of customers and has become the largest internet retailer and marketplace in the world. Through our entrepreneurial culture, Amazon has developed new technologies and products (like Echo) and, enterprise services (like Amazon Web Services).
NOC (Network Operation Center) is the central command and control center for ‘Transportation Execution’ across the Amazon's transportation network. It ensures hassle free, timely pick-up and delivery of freight from vendors to Amazon fulfillment centers (FC) and from Amazon FCs to carrier hubs. In case of any exceptions, NOC steps in to resolve the issue and keeps all the stakeholders informed on the proceedings. Along with this tactical problem solving, NOC is also charged with understanding trends in network exceptions and then automating processes or proposing process changes to streamline operations. This second aspect involves network monitoring and significant analysis of network data.
Overall, NOC plays a critical role in ensuring the smooth functioning of Amazon transportation and thereby has a direct impact on Amazon’s ability to serve its customers on time.

Responsibilities of a NOC PM
We are looking for an experienced Program Manager to coordinate and lead efforts across operations, multiple technology and cross-border program teams. We're looking for a hands-on and motivated self-starter who's passionate about using data to help us measure every area of the business, drive efficiencies, optimizations and influence decision-making. This role is a part of the centralized Network Operations Centre (NOC) org part of Amazon India. This role is based in Dalian, China and will be required to work for Amazon Japan.
A Program Manager is expected to have deep functional knowledge, ability to design new program frameworks/processes and running defect reduction programs. They should be proficient, in identifying the input and output metric to gauge the success of a program. In this role, they will work with business and operations team to analyze historic results, challenge status quo and make business recommendations to senior management based on those analyses – all in an environment of rapid growth and increasing complexity. The Program Manager will drive improvements to the reporting tools, methods, and processes utilized by the team to increase the availability and granularity of actionable data to internal and external partners. The successful candidate must have very strong analytical skills and expert in excel. Knowledge of SQL and tools like R/Python would be an added advantage. They will be experienced at working with large data sets and the technical tools needed to work with them. They will have superb communication and customer-relationship skills, outstanding analytic insight, and be a passionate advocate of operations team to other stakeholders. They will drive towards simple, scalable solutions to difficult problems, have excellent project-management skills, and be able to communicate complex analytical results, both written and verbally, in a clear and easy-to-understand way. title: Contracts & Procurement Spec.,  Supply Chain, Prime Air
descriptionHtml:
Source the Hardware That Powers Drone Delivery

How do you source advanced components for autonomous drones that must meet aerospace safety standards while scaling to millions of deliveries? How do you balance cost, quality, and innovation when working with suppliers across electronics, mechanical systems, and aerospace hardware? Prime Air needs a commodity specialist to solve these challenges.

As a Prime Air - Supply Chain Contracts & Procurement Specialists, you will manage sourcing and supplier relationships for hardware components that power Prime Air's revolutionary drone delivery system. You will execute commodity strategies, negotiate with suppliers, drive orders including procurement ordering/scheduling, analyze spend patterns, and drive cost optimization while ensuring quality and delivery performance. You will work directly with Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain teams to support Prime Air's rapid scaling across the US and Europe.

This is a unique opportunity to work on hardware commodities for a first-of-its-kind business—with Amazon's scale, resources, and innovation culture behind you.

Check out more about Prime Air on the About Amazon blog.


Key job responsibilities
What You'll Own

Manage Hardware Commodity Categories: Own day-to-day commodity management for assigned hardware categories such as electronics, sensors, motors, batteries, mechanical components, or structural materials. Execute sourcing strategies, manage supplier relationships, and drive performance improvements across your categories.

Execute Strategic Sourcing Activities: Conduct RFx processes, evaluate supplier proposals, perform cost analysis, and support contract negotiations. Use spend analysis and benchmarking to identify cost savings opportunities and improve total cost of ownership. Present recommendations to commodity management leadership.

Drive Supplier Performance: Monitor supplier performance on quality, delivery, cost, and responsiveness. Conduct regular business reviews with suppliers, track key performance indicators, and drive corrective actions when needed. Build strong working relationships that enable Prime Air's rapid growth.

Support New Product Introduction: Partner with Engineering teams to identify and qualify suppliers for new hardware components. Evaluate supplier technical capabilities, manufacturing capacity, and quality systems. Support prototype builds, design changes, and production ramps.

Analyze Spend and Market Trends: Track commodity spend patterns, identify cost drivers, and analyze market trends that impact pricing and availability. Develop should-cost models and competitive benchmarks to inform sourcing decisions. Use data to identify opportunities for supplier consolidation and volume leverage.

Ensure Supply Continuity: Monitor supplier health, identify supply chain risks, and develop mitigation plans. Coordinate with suppliers on inventory positioning, lead time management, and capacity planning to support Prime Air's deployment schedules.

title: Technical Account Manager, National Security - ES US-ADC
descriptionHtml:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

National Security customers are moving their most sensitive mission-critical workloads to AWS - and they need a technical advisor who understands both the technology and the stakes. As our Enterprise Support footprint grows across classified environments we're adding a Technical Account Manager (TAM) to meet that demand.

In this role you are the primary technical relationship your National Security customers have at AWS. You'll work hands-on with customers as they adopt services like EC2, S3, DynamoDB, RDS, Lambda, SageMaker, ECS/EKS, GuardDuty, Systems Manager, and Bedrock inside classified environments. You won't troubleshoot tickets directly but you will own the technical health of your accounts: identifying risks before they become incidents guiding architecture decisions and representing AWS in rooms where the margin for error is zero.

Your technical acumen and customer-facing skills will enable you to drive discussions with senior leadership regarding incidents trade-offs support and risk management. You will provide advocacy and strategic technical guidance to help plan and build solutions using best practices and proactively keep your customers' AWS environments operationally healthy.

This is not a sales role. It is a seat at the table with government and defense leaders who rely on your judgment to keep their operations running and evolving. This position will require the ability to travel 10% or more as needed.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph.

Key job responsibilities
• Lead technical engagements by conducting architecture reviews and operational health assessments to keep customer environments resilient and mission-ready.
• Partner with customers to design and implement cloud-native systems that meet the security and compliance demands of classified workloads.
• Identify operational gaps and surface emerging risks working with AWS service teams to resolve issues before they reach production.
• Help customers integrate AI/ML services like SageMaker and Bedrock into their existing workflows turning new technology into practical deployable solutions.
• Advocate for your customers' technical needs across AWS service teams escalation paths and product roadmap discussions.
• Coordinate across internal teams during incidents driving resolution and communicating status to senior stakeholders in real time.

A day in the life
Most of your week is customer-facing. Mondays typically start with cadence calls - reviewing operational metrics checking open action items and setting priorities. Midweek goes deeper: leading Well-Architected reviews walking through architecture proposals or running incident post-mortems with customer engineering teams. When something breaks you coordinate across AWS service teams and communicate status to senior leadership in real time.

Between customer sessions you'll research emerging AWS services relevant to your accounts and collaborate with fellow TAMs on patterns across the national security space. Every customer environment is different and the classified context keeps the work challenging.

title: Senior Regional EHS Manager
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we prioritize health, safety, and well-being above all else. There is nothing more important. To support this priority, Amazon is seeking an experienced and innovative Senior Regional Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) Manager to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for partnering with a regional operations team to execute company WHS policies and ensure compliance to all applicable local, regional and federal regulations. By leveraging lean principles and kaizens, you will lead continuous improvement initiatives to reduce conditional and ergonomic risk to ensure a safe and healthful working environment for Amazon’s Associates.

In this role, you must demonstrate the ability to build trust and confidence with the cross functional operations teams, and influence change through providing comprehensive risk assessments and safety data analysis. To do so, you must be an effective communicator and send clear, concise and consistent messages, both verbally and in writing. You will also be required to instruct and train operations leadership and site WHS professionals in company EHS policies while assisting the regional teams in incorporating our safety standards at their sites. Your experience working in safety programs and your relevant safety, environmental and ergonomic knowledge in an operations environment will be crucial.

You will be responsible for developing a team of safety managers and safety professionals within your designated region. Your teams’ success will depend on your ability to create and execute leadership development plans for your larger team. You must demonstrate your ability to clearly communicate organizational direction through your team and give frequent and appropriate feedback to your WHS teams while ensuring they are executing to the core competencies of an Amazon WHS professional. As a senior leader in the WHS organization, you will also be responsible for judging and assessing safety talent to select appropriate bench strength for current and future business needs.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:
- Act as SME of local/regional regulations and company WHS policy.
- Provide guidance and oversight to ensure compliance to all applicable Amazon WHS Policies.
- Measure the regions and sites’ performance against published requirements in WHS policies. For all deficiencies, identify a plan for the site to implement and fix all identified deficiencies.
- Ensure WHS recordkeeping and data integrity and provides Operations with accurate reporting and metrics to support business WHS initiatives.
- Deliver on-time and quality projects to Operations. Deliver quality projects on time to Operations.
- Analyze WHS metrics and review incident weekly and monthly incident trends to discover trends to justify the allocation of appropriate resources to areas where the safety risk is highest.
- Analyze Global Safety Peer Review results and develop and implement solutions to eliminate exposure to these risks and prevent injury at other FCs.
- Audit recordkeeping practices and Global WHS Database entries to ensure compliance to global WHS standards and local regulations.
- Audit the workplace organization and Associate behaviors to ensure that training, auditing and scoring methods are accurate and consistent.
- Manage and mentor the FC WHS Manager and WHS Associates in your assigned FCs.
- Spend time at the fulfillment centers and seek input from WHS teams, Associates and leaders on WHS program improvement opportunities. Ensure open communication on status of progress and resolution against these suggestions.
- Lead soft tissue injury reduction efforts by performing targeted Kaizens in partnership with the Operations teams based on the risks identified in each task (force, repetition, and awkward postures).
- Ensure site leadership and Associates are trained and knowledgeable of their responsibilities under each policy. Audit the quality, delivery (including qualifications of the trainer), and effectiveness of all required WHS training.
- Review for effectiveness the deployed WHS tools and revise to ensure continual improvement.
- Partner with corporate and other regional field WHS personnel to leverage global WHS and environmental best practices into NA network standards.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site

Those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 7+ years of increasing responsibilities in safety and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, service operations, or relevant experience applicable to the role
- 7+ years of increasing responsibilities in people and performance management
- Experience implementing lean principles and process improvement in an operational environment.
- Ability to travel up to 50%
- Office within one of the designated region's sites. Must be willing to relocate if not currently within region
- Willingness to work a variety of shifts, including nights and weekends, as required to support direct reports and site needs.

Preferred qualifications

- Master’s degree preferred
- Certified Safety Professional preferred
- Experience in a fast-paced, dynamic organization
- Interest in long-term career development through assignments in multiple business units across the nation
- Prior experience in a management development training program
- Track record of effectively managing a safety operation comprising both salaried and hourly staff
- Demonstrate experience in developing others into higher levels of responsibility in an organization
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort interfacing with Directors and VPs.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

title: Senior Program Manager, 3P Seafood Distribution, Whole Foods Market
descriptionHtml:
Whole Foods Market (WFM) sources seafood through a complex network of third-party distributors whose performance directly determines what customers find on the shelf. This role owns that network, from the contracts that govern it, the relationships that sustain it, and the strategic path forward for how WFM partners with 3Ps to meet quality, availability, and cost-to-serve goals at scale. You will be the single-threaded owner for 3P seafood distributor contract management and performance and the strategic architect helping WFM define what the right 3P model looks like going forward. This means owning both the operational rigor (contract terms, service levels, compliance) and the longer-horizon strategic thinking, challenging assumptions about how WFM's seafood distribution network should be structured to protect quality differentiation and supply security over the long-term.

This is a high-visibility, high-complexity role that sits at the intersection of Procurement, Inventory Planning, Store Operations, Finance, and Supplier Partnerships. The right candidate brings deep distributor contract experience, strong financial modeling skills, and the credibility to lead WFM's 3P strategy in a perishable’s environment where margin, quality, and supply continuity are non-negotiable.


Key job responsibilities
3P Seafood Distributor Contract Management & Negotiations
•Own the full lifecycle of 3P seafood distributor contracts: from initial scoping, RFP/RFQ, and negotiation through execution, renewal, amendment, and termination. This includes fee structures, service-level agreements, delivery schedules, quality standards, cold-chain requirements, and cost-to-serve terms.
•Lead negotiations on rate increases, new service charges, and contract amendments: building and defending WFM's counter-position with documented cost offsets, volume commitments, and business case modeling. When distributors issue unilateral rate changes, own the response framework and resolution.
•Develop and maintain a contract management framework: renewal timelines, escalation triggers, performance benchmarks, and obligation tracking across all active 3P seafood distributor relationships. Maintain centralized repository of key terms, expiration dates, and open obligations.
•Monitor distributor performance against contractual obligations: fill rates, on-time delivery, EDI compliance (including ASN accuracy), cold-chain integrity, and spec adherence. Quantify gaps, drive resolution, and escalate when underperformance creates store-level or financial risk.
•Partner with Finance to model contract economics: total cost of distribution, landed cost impact by distributor, and financial exposure from service failures or contract changes. Build business cases for contract restructuring, consolidation, or termination decisions.

3P Strategy & Path Forward for WFM
•Lead the development of WFM's 3P seafood distributor strategy: defining what the right distributor model looks like across a 2–3 year horizon. This includes evaluating distributor consolidation opportunities, exclusivity arrangements, delivery frequency optimization, co-investment structures, and how 3P relationships ladder up to WFM's quality, supply security, and cost-to-serve goals.
•Assess current 3P distributor network against WFM's regional supply requirements: identify coverage gaps, redundancies, cost-to-serve inefficiencies, and capability constraints (e.g., cold-chain infrastructure, processing capacity, delivery frequency). Translate findings into actionable network design recommendations.
•Design and manage distributor onboarding and qualification frameworks: defining the standards (quality, compliance, EDI, cold-chain, financial stability) new 3P partners must meet before going live. Own the go-live process for new distributor relationships including cross-functional readiness (Procurement, IP, Store Ops, Finance).
•Identify and evaluate opportunities for strategic 3P partnerships: including exclusivity arrangements, co-investment in processing or logistics capacity, and multi-year supply commitments that create competitive advantage for WFM. Build and present business cases to leadership for partnership structures that go beyond transactional distribution agreements.
•Serve as WFM's primary point of escalation and resolution when distributor relationships reach inflection points: contract disputes, service failures, unilateral cost actions, or capacity constraints that threaten store-level availability. Own the resolution playbook and the outcome.

Distributor Performance Management & Compliance
•Build and own the 3P distributor scorecard: tracking performance across fill rate, on-time delivery, EDI/ASN compliance, invoice accuracy, spec adherence, and cold-chain integrity. Use scorecard data to drive accountability conversations, renegotiations, and network-level decisions.
•Own the delivery schedule coordination process between 3P distributors and WFM DCs: ensuring schedule changes are communicated cross-functionally to Procurement, Inventory Planning, and Store Operations before store-facing communications go out. Prevent coordination failures that create downstream supply risk.
•Manage distributor compliance with WFM quality standards, animal welfare certifications, and labeling/documentation requirements. Escalate spec violations with financial impact quantification and a defined remediation timeline. Ensure compliance failures are resolved — not absorbed silently.

Cross-Functional Alignment & Stakeholder Management
•Serve as the connective tissue between 3P distributors and WFM's internal functions of Procurement, Inventory Planning, Store Operations, Finance, and Legal. Ensure distributor commitments are operationally real and that internal teams have what they need to execute against them.
•Lead cross-functional working sessions to resolve distributor-related conflicts, align on go-live readiness, and unblock execution. Develop and deliver executive-level communications on distributor contract status, negotiation outcomes, strategic recommendations, and path-forward options.
•Manage competing priorities across DC Operations, Finance, and Supplier teams to maintain program momentum on distributor transitions, new go-lives, and contract renegotiations. Document program outcomes, lessons learned, and playbooks for future distributor management.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree, or MBA in business, operations, human resources, adult education, organizational development, instructional design or related field
- Knowledge of general AI tools
- Experience designing, implementing, and scaling upskilling, apprenticeship, or workforce development programs across large-scale operations or corporate environments, including forecasting workforce needs and leveraging analytics to drive program decisions

title: Sr. Software Development Engineer, Device Software and Services (DS2)
descriptionHtml:
The Cloud Connectivity and Management Services (C2MS) organization, within Device Software and Services (DS2), owns the end-to-end solutions to connect, communicate, keep up to date, and manage all Amazon-powered devices through the Amazon Cloud. Our services handle persistent device-to-cloud connectivity, bidirectional Device Messaging, Over-the-Air software updates, and Remote Settings Management at a scale of hundreds of millions of devices across multiple regions.

Being part of the Device Messaging team means that the software we build is used by every person you know who owns an Amazon Device, and by dozens of external partners that send messages to our devices. The scale and reach we present at Amazon is a unique opportunity to directly influence the experience of millions of customers around the world. We own the complete end-to-end Device Messaging experience for all Amazon devices. We enable guaranteed delivery of push notifications, synchronous request-response messaging, and device-to-cloud communication for dozens of internal 1P teams (Echo, Fire TV, Kindle, Tablets), platform teams, and hundreds of third-party applications.

As a Senior SDE on this team, you will be a technical leader who defines the ideal customer experience for users of our Device Messaging services. You will drive innovation in messaging solutions, and define the end-to-end experience of our customers, including observability, data analytics, message delivery insights, and customer action analytics to make our platform best-in-class. You will architect complex distributed systems, set technical direction, and establish architectural principles for the team. You will partner with engineering leaders and product managers to shape the roadmap. You will be a force multiplier, mentoring engineers, raising the technical bar, and fostering a culture of engineering and operational excellence. Additionally, you will consult across other C2MS teams, including Remote Settings and Over-the-Air Updates, to help solve complex cross-cutting technical challenges.

Key job responsibilities
- Architect and deliver complex software systems that align with Amazon's engineering standards and business objectives.
- Drive technical decisions and design reviews that impact multiple services or teams within the organization.
- Lead development of critical features while mentoring junior engineers in technical best practices and engineering principles.
- Establish and maintain robust monitoring, metrics, and operational excellence practices for high-availability systems.
- Define and enforce code quality standards, testing strategies, and documentation requirements across projects.
- Proactively identify and resolve complex technical challenges while implementing preventive measures.
- Participate in building high-performing teams through technical interviews and making data-driven hiring recommendations.

A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing a technical design document from a teammate, providing feedback that strengthens the approach before a broader design review. Later, you dive into code, perhaps refactoring a critical component to improve extensibility or prototyping an interface that defines boundaries between services. After lunch, you join a cross-team discussion to resolve a dependency conflict, building consensus on a path that balances both teams' needs. You wrap up by pairing with a junior engineer on a tricky debugging session, turning it into a coaching moment.

About the team
We are building teams with Amazon DNA in Guadalajara, Mexico: two-pizza teams who are the single-threaded owners of their end-to-end experience. You will be the only team responsible for defining all architectural decisions, implementation, testing, and operational excellence for Amazon Device Messaging. We are looking for customer-obsessed engineers who are passionate about innovating on behalf of customers, demonstrate a high degree of technical ownership, and want to make history. It is still Day 1 in the Devices business, and we are seeking a creative problem-solver with exceptional judgment and the ability to deliver results under ambiguous circumstances and tight timelines.

- 8+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 8+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience

- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

Preferred qualifications

title: Sr. Program Manager, Workplace Health & Safety, WHS Central Programs Team
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) mission is to provide tools, resources, and environments that support safe, efficient, and healthy behaviors and encourage employees to proactively manage their health and wellbeing. To support this focus area, Amazon is seeking a leader to serve as our Program Manager for Worldwide WHS to build programs that create a safe workplace and build a world-class safety culture. In this role, you will dive deep into operations processes; identify risks through data and first-hand experience; build programs and improve processes to eliminate risks; and influence operations to sustain a culture of safety. This role will focus on leading large, strategic projects within Amazon Business Units (BU) and across different geographies – the role will also look for ways to replicate these BU-specific solutions to other BU, and find commonalities to support scale and speed.
The Sr. Program manager role will challenge you to push boundaries and lead transformative innovation while having the autonomy to make rapid data-driven decisions and invent on behalf of Operators (leaders) and Associates. In this role, you will work cross-functionally with members from various teams, including Operations; Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT); Amazon Robotics (AR); Inbound Supply Chain; Launch; Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP); Capacity Planning; Finance and others to deploy solutions at scale.

This position requires travel up to approximately 25% when needed (and with appropriate health and safety conditions).



Key job responsibilities
The ideal candidate:
- Owns and drives safety programs from inception through global implementation, delivering measurable injury and risk reduction outcomes across Amazon's worldwide network.
- Leads and manages safety-related projects end-to-end, defining clear actions, owners, and timelines to ensure successful delivery.
- Authors narrative papers and business reviews for senior leadership audiences, clearly communicating safety priorities, program performance, and investment recommendations
- Serves as a trusted safety partner to regional leaders, aligning on strategic priorities and tracking progress against goals
- Conducts regular site visits to fulfillment centers, sortation facilities, and delivery stations to personally observe safety practices, gather front-line feedback, and identify opportunities for improvement
- Leads comprehensive incident investigations, rapidly identifying root causes and implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence and share learnings globally
- Collaborates cross-functionally with teams in Operations, Engineering, HR, and beyond to scale successful safety initiatives and embed sustainable improvements
- Monitors safety metrics, analyze trends, and present data-driven recommendations to senior leadership on priorities and investment areas


A day in the life
As a Program Manager on the WHS Central Programs Team (CPT), your day centers on project management best practices applied to safety. Expect to spend your time reviewing safety data, running working sessions to unblock in-flight projects, and walking through operational processes to ground your decisions in field truth. You will drive projects that move from idea to validated, network-wide deployment, by working closely with BU stakeholders across the globe.

About the team
The WHS Central Programs Team (CPT) delivers projects that directly impact associate safety. This team dives deep into operational processes, leverages data to identify risks, initiates project ideas, and enhances existing processes. Collaborating closely with field operations, WHS personnel, Tech teams, engineering teams and additional stakeholders, the Central Programs Team employs project management best practices to address defined safety related issues. Furthermore, the Central Programs Team assumes direct responsibility for project definition, piloting, and the deployment of validated projects into the network.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in program or project management
- Experience using data and metrics to measure impact and determine improvements
- Experience in written and spoken English and an ability to compose grammatically correct, concise and accurate written responses
- Experience in safety and/or environmental programs in manufacturing, production, service operations, or related fields
- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, safety, environment, or equivalent field of study

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing projects and working independently
- Experience working within a global company, with multi-country responsibilities
- Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.)
- Experience in technical writing in a relevant field
- Knowledge of regulatory requirements and the ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 standards
- NEBOSH, IOSH, CHMM, ASP, CSP, or CIH certification
- Fluency in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools

descriptionHtml:
There’s a universe of opportunity at Amazon.

At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates,

services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and
connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact.

operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and
launch solutions that matter. With endless opportunities to explore
across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and
discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment
designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the
world. Ready to start your adventure?

What’s in it for you?
An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll
build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed,
while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.



Key job responsibilities
As an Operations Engineer Intern, you could have the opportunity to join one of the following teams: Project Management, Change Management, People Management, Planning, Contracting Management, Infrastructure, Reliability Maintenance Engineering and more. You will work on a project with real impact within Amazon. This could include:

Design, build, improve, and innovate order fulfilment infrastructure throughout the large-scale supply chain network.

Manage, design, and implement small to medium scope integrated automation projects with system elements such as high-speed sortation, multiple conveyors, package lines, and/or robotic work cells.

Support within the EU Controls network on a project to enhance the capability to monitor MHE metrics and provide visualization and data to internal customers.

Working on a program to train technicians in the basics of control systems fault finding to raise the level of knowledge within the site.

Every day is different as an Operations Engineer Intern. You'll work alongside experienced engineers on real projects that design, build, and improve fulfilment infrastructure across Amazon's large-scale supply chain network. You might spend your morning analysing MHE performance data and developing visualisations to help teams monitor equipment metrics, then spend your afternoon on the warehouse floor supporting the installation and commissioning of new automation equipment. You will collaborate with global teams, interface with stakeholders at all levels, and drive solutions with real operational impact.

Amazon's fulfilment network relies on cutting-edge technology — from robotics and high-speed sortation to conveyance systems and robotic work cells. No matter which team you join, whether it's Project Management, Reliability Maintenance Engineering, Controls, or Infrastructure, part of your role will involve solving complex engineering challenges. Opportunities:

Upon successful completion of the internship, you may be considered for a graduate role or a second internship, allowing you to continue your journey with Amazon. Additionally, you'll enjoy a competitive monthly salary, relocation support, and access to a range of employee benefits.

- Currently in your final or penultimate year and working towards a university bachelors’ or masters’ degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Automation, Industrial or Software), or a STEM subject.

title: Senior Software Development Engineer (Tech L), DSO (Demand Science Optimization)
descriptionHtml:
Senior Software Development Engineer driving the re-architecture of Amazon Devices' pricing and assortment planning platform — the system that decides what devices sell where, when, and at what price, across every Amazon device sold worldwide. This role owns the design and delivery of a new domain-modeled system: collapsing a fragmented legacy input pipeline into an automated platform that determines pricing and retailer placement for over 21,000 products across 7 device families and 22+ countries.

The team's scope is growing, and you will shape how it grows.

What you will work on:

- Setting technical direction and architecture across the services the team owns
- Raising the engineering bar through design review, code review, and operational standards
- Aligning with engineers on partner teams on shared interfaces and ownership boundaries
- Replacing recurring manual work with automation and better design
- Mentoring engineers as they grow into deeper technical ownership

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, and operate the most technically complex parts of the input layer, using AI-assisted development and agents to replace work that is manual today
- Set technical direction and architecture, including decisions to consolidate, rebuild, or retire systems
- Lead design and code reviews, and define the operational standards a service meets before the team owns it
- Partner with product managers, scientists, and engineers on other teams to turn requirements into designs and to align on shared interfaces and ownership boundaries
- Mentor engineers through design guidance, written documentation, and pairing

A day in the life
Your primary focus is the layer of inputs that Amazon's device planning, forecasting, and inventory systems all read from. A handful of services, and every build and allocation decision downstream depends on them agreeing.

You're rebuilding that layer to easily allow stakeholders to manage a whole product line's inputs for high-impact decisions. You'll make the calls on what that architecture looks like.

Beyond this system, an Sr. SDE in DSO is expected to operate across charters — bringing technical judgment to whichever part of the org needs it most at a given time, representing the team in cross-charter design discussions, and mentoring engineers across projects.

About the team
We own the inputs Amazon's device planning, forecasting, and inventory systems depend on — the data behind what gets built, where it ships, and at what price. Our customers are internal: the planners who own each product line, finance partners, and the science and engineering teams downstream. You'll work with them directly.
We're rebuilding it so each input lives in one place and stays correct without someone tending it, moving toward agent-based interfaces.

Basic qualifications

- 7+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 7+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
- 7+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team

Preferred qualifications

- 7+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Engineer Operations Technician , DCEO Operations Team
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability

Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)

Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)

Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA

Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment

Technical writing to support change management program

Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion

On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation

Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.

Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:

Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:

Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently

Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds

Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder

Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position

Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:

Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed

Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

- 2+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance, or 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience

We are looking for motivated, customer-focused individuals who want to join our team as an Operations Manager. In this role, you will lead and develop a team of salaried and hourly talent. title: Data Center Controls Engineer, Queretaro
descriptionHtml:
As part of the global controls team, you will work with highly motivated experts and innovators in the data center industry. You will be responsible for troubleshooting, project management, and maintaining the building management system (BMS) and electrical power monitoring system (EPMS). Using Amazon leadership principles, you will develop new processes and standards while innovating in the controls space. AWS Data centers have multiple components such as generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switch-gear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers [air-cooled and water-cooled], pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers, etc. All these components have local control systems that interact with each other via open and/or proprietary communications protocols. The BMS is the primary method of control of all mechanical systems within a data center. The EPMS is the primary method of monitoring all electrical systems within a data center.

Key job responsibilities
1. Complex Multi-System Management & Technical Support - Responsible for the entire lifecycle of BMS and EPMS systems including creation, design, configuration, validation, installation, commissioning, operation, and ongoing troubleshooting across multiple data centers.
2. Project Management Under Constraints - Must develop and manage project scope, schedules, budgets, and level of efforts while juggling multiple stakeholder deliverables and navigating challenging situations with competing requirements.
3. Emergency Response & Critical System Support - Required to participate in AWS global on-call schedule to provide immediate technical support to in-service data centers, demanding constant availability.
4. Extensive Vendor & Procurement Coordination - Involves managing procurement activities (RFQs, RFPs, RFIs, purchase orders), financially managing service contracts, and supervising vendor work to ensure compliance with specifications and codes.
5. Frequent Travel & On-Site Presence - Must frequently visit locally assigned data centers (both operational and under construction) for troubleshooting, customer meetings, and vendor supervision, requiring significant time away from desk work.
