title: Operations Engineer, Mechatronics Technical Trainer, Material Handling Equipment Systems, OneMHS
descriptionHtml:
Are you a hands-on technical instructor who thrives at the intersection of engineering and education? Amazon is building a new training organization within our Installation and Deployment team, and we need a versatile Operations Engineer to help shape it from the ground up. As the team scales to support a growing network of fulfillment facilities, you will develop, deliver, and continuously improve technical training programs for material handling equipment (MHE) — spanning conveyor systems, sortation equipment, and associated automation infrastructure.

You will combine classroom and field-based instruction with video production and digital learning development, translating complex installation procedures into clear, scalable content. Working closely with Mechanical Integration Leads (MILs), Electrical Installation Leads (EILs), and field execution teams, you will capture real-world scenarios and turn them into training that reflects how systems actually come together on site. This is a rare opportunity to join a newer organization where your contributions will directly shape the standards, processes, and culture of the team.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and deliver hands-on and classroom-based technical training across mechanical, electrical, and controls disciplines for MHE installation crews, field technicians, and integration leads — covering topics from structural steel placement and conveyor alignment through power distribution, device commissioning, and quality control procedures.
- Record, edit, and produce professional training videos and digital learning modules using industry-standard tools, building out the organization's training library with content grounded in real field scenarios and best practices.
- Collaborate with MILs, EILs, controls engineers, and field execution teams to identify training gaps, validate technical accuracy, and align training schedules with site deployment timelines so crews are prepared ahead of mobilization.
- Partner with the Technical Training Lead to prioritize content development based on deployment schedules, incident reports, and field feedback — driving continuous improvement of training effectiveness and operational readiness.
- Define and track success metrics for training programs, including completion rates and competency progression, while developing Standard Work Instructions and installation standard operating procedures to support consistent execution across sites.

A day in the life
Your morning might start in a training room walking technicians through conveyor mechanical alignment using hands-on demonstrations and e-learning pre-work you built. After the session, you head to the installation floor to record conduit installation and wire termination procedures for a new training video. In the afternoon, you are editing footage into a polished module or building an online course complete with annotated field photos and scenario-based exercises. You close out by syncing with your Training Lead on upcoming site visits and flagging a training gap surfaced by a recent incident report.

About the team
We are a newer organization within Amazon's Installation and Deployment team, focused on building the training function that will support MHE installation across a rapidly scaling fulfillment network. Our mission is to ensure every field crew has the knowledge and confidence to execute safely and efficiently. As we grow, you will have the opportunity to shape processes, define standards, and take on broader responsibilities in an environment where your ideas carry real weight. We work cross-functionally with engineering, operations, and field execution teams, and we are looking for collaborative, self-starting team members who are excited to build something new.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in the mechanical or controls field, or experience working with electrical and mechanical conveyance systems

- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings, or experience in electrical or mechanical engineering
- Experience developing and delivering training programs, or experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities
- Knowledge of Photoshop, video editing, and related tools
- 2+ years of maintenance or engineering experience
- Associate's degree in a technical field, or 3+ years of Amazon RME (Reliability Maintenance Engineering) BB/3P Full Time Exempt experience
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays

title: Senior Financial Analyst, RME Finance, WW Ops
descriptionHtml:
RME Finance Analysts own cost across the network. They provide FP&A support for North America Field RME teams, covering MEC, controllership, and operational planning cycles. Success in this role requires intellectual curiosity, comfort with ambiguity, and a genuine drive to improve how work gets done.

Key job responsibilities
- Run Month End Close for Personnel and Parts, Repairs, and Maintenance (PRM) accounts. You are accountable for accuracy, completeness, and controllership compliance from start to finish.

- Own the financial planning cycles, including forecast modeling, bridging, and variance analysis. You work with limited guidance and are expected to identify cost drivers and bring clear findings to senior managers.

- Deliver data-driven narratives that shape how leaders make decisions. Push back on business partner plans when the numbers tell a different story.

- Manage controllership for headcount and Coupa. When you see a gap, you fix it. Hold yourself and the process to a high standard.

- Build relationships across Field and Central RME, Finance, and Operations. Your credibility comes from the quality of your work and trust built over time.

- Find ways to make the work better. Lead process improvement projects, document what you learn, and share across the team.

- Use AI and automation to handle routine work. The goal is to spend time on work that actually matters.

- Use QuickSight, Cognos, and other internal systems to surface insights from financial and productivity data.

- Help grow the people around you—contribute to onboarding, share knowledge, and be a resource for junior teammates.

A day in the life
The FP&A work is cyclical. MEC runs Days 1-5 each month, with five budget cycles per year. That core work is non-negotiable. But about 15% of your time is spent on harder, less-defined problems—that's where the real opportunity is.

RME is one of Amazon's fastest-growing organizations. You'll be in the middle of the AI, robotics, and automation buildout across Stores sites. You'll partner with network leaders, influence how cost is managed in the field, and continuously look for ways to automate what doesn't need a human.

No two days look the same.

About the team
The team supports Field RME across North America Consumer Fulfillment (NACF), Amazon Transportation Services (ATS), and Global Delivery Services (GDS), along with the Worldwide (WW) RME Central Team.

- Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting or related field
- 3+ years of finance or a related analytical field experience
- 3+ years of contributing to cross-functional initiatives that drive financial performance and strategy experience
- 3 years of experience dissecting financial data and identifying patterns that support business strategy

title: Security Operations Engineer, AWS Security Cloud Response
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is looking for a focused Security Engineer who can take on a leadership role in responding to security issues across the largest cloud provider in the world. The right candidate must thrive in high-pressure situations, think like both an attacker and defender, and drive relevant teams to take the right actions in the right timeframes to mitigate risks.

We are looking for an individual who can balance technical risks against business risks and consistently drive for the right results. They must have the passion for engineering novel solutions to complex security challenges, and recognize and fill gaps in capabilities. The ability to quickly design and build internal-facing tools that enable scaled programmatic automation is a plus.

The successful candidate will have a good mix of deep technical knowledge and a demonstrated background in information security. We value broad and deep technical knowledge, specifically in the fields of cryptography, network security, software security, malware analysis, forensics, security operations, incident response, and emergent security intelligence.

An ideal candidate should be able to accomplish most of the following:
- Confidently and intelligently respond to security incidents, and proactively consider how to prevent the same type of incidents from occurring in the future.

- Design and coordinate cohesive responses to security events that involve multiple teams across the organization.

- Build security utilities and tools for internal use that enable you and your fellow Security Engineers to operate at high speed and wide scale.

- Evaluate the impact to the organization of current security trends, advisories, publications, and academic research. Coordinate responses as necessary across affected teams to do the right thing for our customers and our organization.

- Ability to communicate effectively at multiple levels of sensitivity, and multiple audiences.

- Recognize, adopt and instill the best practices in security engineering fields throughout the organization: development, cryptography, network security, security operations, incident response, security intelligence.

- Provide subject matter expertise on architecture, authentication and system security.

- Fulfill regular on-call responsibilities.

Key job responsibilities
An ideal candidate should be able to accomplish most of the following:

- Triage/assess security issues and engage with internal service teams to ensure timely remediation of issues, escalating internally as necessary to ensure appropriate levels of urgency and engagement.
- Participate in efforts to promote security throughout the Company and build good working relationships within the team and with others across Amazon.
- Demonstrate high capacity and tolerance for context switching and interruptions while remaining productive and effective.
- Develop pragmatic solutions that achieve business requirements while maintaining an acceptable level of risk.
- Mentoring of junior staff and proactively share knowledge sharing within the team and across the company.
- Assist with hiring new employees
- Fulfil regular on-call responsibilities.

A day in the life
AWS Cloud Response is responsible for the security of AWS Cloud services. Our primary focus is to ensure the security of the cloud by working with service teams, vendors, and other stakeholders (both internal and external) to solve security challenges at massive scale, from incident response to emergent patching to helping publish guidance for customer impacting issues. We also work to develop tools and systems, and implement changes to drive automation, scalability and continuous improvements for our organization and AWS as a whole.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Knowledge of networking protocols such as HTTP, DNS and TCP/IP
- Experience programming in Python, Ruby, Go, Swift, Java, .Net, C++ or similar object oriented language
- Information security professional certification
- Knowledge of system security vulnerabilities and remediation techniques, including penetration testing and the development of exploits or equivalent
- Experience applying threat modeling or other risk identification techniques or equivalent
- Experience implementing security solutions at the business division level or equivalent
- This role requires you to be a national of an EU member state.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with AWS products and services
- Experience with any combination of the following: threat modeling, secure coding, identity management and authentication, software development, cryptography, system administration and network security
- Experience with programming languages such as Python, Java, C++
- Experience in security operations, risk management, and incident response

title: Automation Engineering Apprentice - North East (48-month fixed term contract)
descriptionHtml:
Ever wondered what it's like to orchestrate a symphony of robots? Picture yourself at the controls of one of the world's most sophisticated automated networks - where thousands of robots work in perfect harmony, artificial intelligence makes split-second decisions, and breakthrough technology comes to life. This isn't science fiction. This is Amazon, and it could be your everyday workspace as an Automation Apprentice.

Our fulfilment centres are like living, breathing cities of automation: hundreds of autonomous robots collaborating to fulfil customer orders, AI and machine-learning systems making real-time decisions, conveyor systems spanning miles, robotic arms handling packages with incredible precision, and automated storage and retrieval systems redefining what efficiency looks like. As an Automation Apprentice within our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team, you'll be hands-on with technology most people only read about, working alongside industry pioneers. This isn't just maintenance - it's being part of a team that innovates, improves, and reimagines automation technology every single day, with the chance to see your own ideas come to life in real-world applications.

Are you the person who took things apart to see how they worked? Maybe you built a PC, fixed everyone's tech, loved robotics club or Lego Technic, tinkered with a car or bike, or found physics, electronics or design and technology just clicked. Or maybe you've spent a few years in a hands-on role and want to step up into cutting-edge automation. You don't need to be an engineer already - what matters is curiosity about how things work, a logical, problem-solving mind, and the patience to figure out why something's gone wrong and put it right. If that sounds like you, this could be the start of something extraordinary.

A day in the life can involve:
- Supporting maintenance and fault-finding on automated systems and robotics
- Using diagnostic tools to keep conveyors and sortation equipment running smoothly
- Planning preventative maintenance and safety checks
- Collaborating with engineers to develop new process improvements and energy-efficient solutions

Throughout your apprenticeship, you'll gain both theoretical knowledge and hands-on experience across:
- Advanced robotics systems, controls, and industrial automation programming
- Smart sensor technology and IoT integration
- Predictive maintenance and performance optimisation through data analytics
- Safety systems for human-robot collaboration
- Machine learning applications and wider Industry 4.0 technologies

Here at Amazon, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Within this apprenticeship, you'll learn by doing, putting newfound knowledge into practice every day. Our first-class coaching, tailored development opportunities, and challenging, rewarding work will empower you to reach new heights. If you're a curious learner eager to grow, this is your chance to unlock your full potential and build the future you envision.

Within this 48-month programme, you'll work towards the Level 6 Control Technical Support Apprenticeship, combining practical, on-the-job experience with industry-recognised study. Your first 12 months will be a full-time residential programme, based either at one of our external training provider facilities or at our own world-class Amazon training centres - reflecting our significant investment in developing state-of-the-art facilities for the next generation of engineers. If you live outside a commutable distance, accommodation will be provided during term time for these first 12 months, and travel expenses will be supported. In later years, your on-the-job training will work towards a BSc in Controls and Automation Engineering and an HNC/D in Electrical/Controls Engineering.

This role supports our 24/7 operation, so you'll work shifts covering days, nights and weekends - patterns that reflect the real-world schedules of the engineers who keep Amazon operating around the clock.

You'll join a diverse and passionate team of engineers dedicated to driving results and pushing creative boundaries. We value different perspectives and experiences, and we're dedicated to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. Our employee-led affinity groups - including communities for women in tech, LGBTQ+ employees, and underrepresented minorities - foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to be proud of our differences. These groups provide community, mentorship, and a platform for your voice to be heard. We're committed to building a workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve.

We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a well-rounded professional.

The robots are waiting - are you ready to take control? Turn your passion for technology into an extraordinary career at the forefront of engineering innovation. Apply now and be part of the team writing the future of automation.

Basic qualifications

- To qualify for this programme, you must:
- Be 18 years or over before the start date (September 2027)
- Have the right to live and work in England at the point of enrolment (June 2027). If you are on a visa, this must enable you to legally work and reside in England for the entire duration of the programme from enrolment.
- Have lived in the UK or in the European Economic Area (EEA) for the last 3 years prior to the start date
- Not be registered to study on a UK government funded course ending August 2027 or later
- Be prepared to travel for external/mandatory training as part of the apprenticeship
- 5 GCSEs at grade 4-9 (A-C) or above (or equivalent) including Maths and English.
- Three A levels (or equivalent) at C (grade 4) or above in either Mathematics, IT, Physics, or an Engineering related subject, OR have completed a BTEC level 3 engineering qualification of 180 credits which must include further mathematics
- Please note, if you have received educational qualifications outside of the UK then we will require a Statement of Comparability to confirm your eligibility for the scheme. Please ensure you obtain one during the application process, through UK ENIC: https://www.enic.org.uk/
- Previous qualifications will be reviewed for funding eligibility and offers are subject to funding approval
- PLEASE NOTE: This position is a 48 month fixed-term contract. You must NOT already have a qualification in a similar subject at the same or higher level than this apprenticeship.
- This Apprenticeship assumes the candidate has some or little knowledge/experience of the occupation

Preferred qualifications

- A genuine interest in robotics, automation or engineering - whether that's through a hobby, a project, a club, or simply a habit of taking things apart to understand how they work
- A foundation in a STEM subject such as physics, electronics, design and technology, maths or computing (through school, college, self-study or a previous role)
- Confidence with basic diagnostic or problem-solving approaches - the instinct to work out why something has gone wrong, not just that it has

- Excellent communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate across a busy, fast-paced operation

title: Future Operations Leader - Degree Apprenticeship Scotland (48-month fixed term contract)
descriptionHtml:
Are you ready to step into a leadership role in one of the world's most fast-paced, customer-obsessed operations? This is your opportunity to earn a fully funded degree from while leading in the heart of Amazon's operations - from day one.

Amazon is looking for ambitious, driven individuals to join our Future Operations Leader Degree Apprenticeship. You'll earn a fully funded BA (Hons) in Business Management while working on the ground in one of our fulfilment centres or operational sites, solving real business challenges alongside experienced leaders. This is a hands-on role, not a desk job - our sites are vast (some the size of several football pitches), and you'll be out across the floor where the action happens, covering real distance as you lead teams, drive change, and make a tangible impact.

At its core, this is a people role. Yes, you'll work with data, processes, and technology - but the heart of operations leadership is people. You'll learn how to motivate a team at 3am, how to have difficult conversations with empathy, how to recognise when someone's struggling, and how to create an environment where people want to do their best work. If you're energised by working with others and want to build your career around leading teams, this programme will give you the foundation to do exactly that.

This role involves shift work, including days, nights, and weekends, because our operations run around the clock and great leaders need to understand every part of that rhythm. You'll rotate through different shift patterns, which means early starts, late finishes, and yes, night shifts. It's a demanding, fast-paced environment with a lot to juggle – you'll need to prioritise quickly, stay composed under pressure, and keep the most important things moving. It's a real step up, and we're looking for people who expect that challenge and are ready to run with it. It's a physical, on-your-feet role - you'll be out on the floor, not behind a desk. It's not for everyone, but if you thrive where no two days feel the same and you want to understand operations from the ground up, it's one of the most valuable parts of the experience.

A day in the life can involve:

- Starting with a team stand-up or shift handover, reviewing priorities, performance metrics, and issues from the previous shift

- Shadowing or supporting a team leader or manager on the floor, getting stuck into real-time problem solving - clearing a bottleneck, supporting a team member, or managing workflow across the site

- Working on a project linked to your degree - building a business case for a process improvement, mapping stakeholders for a site change, or analysing quality and risk data to present back to leadership

- On university weeks, attending masterclasses or webinars and completing coursework, then bringing what you've learned straight back onto the floor

As you progress, you'll build relationships across the site, develop your own leadership style, and take on increasing responsibility.

This could be for you if you're the person who captained a sports team, coached younger students, led a group project, completed your Duke of Edinburgh, volunteered in your community, organised something no one asked you to, or put your hand up to be a prefect. Or maybe you've spent a few years in the workplace and found yourself naturally stepping up - training new starters, leading a team, improving a process, or taking ownership of something bigger than your job description. Leadership isn't about a job title; it's about what you do when no one's told you to. If that sounds like you, this programme is your next step.

Over 48 months, you'll develop the knowledge and skills to lead in a complex operational environment, including:

- Business strategy and how organisations operate

- Project planning, scheduling, budgeting, and delivery within time, cost, and quality constraints

- Leading and managing diverse teams, building trust, and driving performance

- Financial controls, business case development, and performance reporting

- Stakeholder engagement, communication, and influencing at all levels

- Organisational change management - preparing teams and operations for change

- Risk identification, quality assurance, and continuous improvement

- Commercial awareness, procurement, and contract management

- Digital innovation, data-driven technologies, and AI in a business context

What you'll achieve:

- BA (Hons) Business Management

- CMI-aligned course content, giving you a route to apply for CMI Chartered Manager accreditation on completion

This is a blended learning programme combining pre-reading and preparation, in-person masterclasses, online learning and webinars, and individual study and assignment writing. You'll be supported throughout by a dedicated Academic Mentor, with progress reviews involving your Line Manager, plus full access to university resources including library services, wellbeing support, and student societies.

Basic qualifications

- To qualify for this programme, you must:
- Be 18 years or over before the start date (September 2027)
- Have the right to live and work in Scotland at the point of enrolment (June 2027). If you are on a visa, this must enable you to legally work and reside in Scotland for the entire duration of the programme from enrolment.
- Have lived in the UK or in the European Economic Area (EEA) for the last 3 years prior to the start date
- Not be registered to study on a UK government funded course ending August 2027 or later
- Be prepared to travel for external/mandatory training as part of the apprenticeship
- Have one of the following:
- Have UCAS Tariff 114, or Scottish Highers AABBB (or equivalent)
- A Foundation Apprenticeship (counts as one Higher at grade B)
- A Modern Apprenticeship at SCQF Level 6 in a relevant discipline (counts as two Highers at grade B)
- Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) - relevant work experience considered in place of formal qualifications; can also place you into a later year of the degree"
- Please note, if you have received educational qualifications outside of the UK then we will require a Statement of Comparability to confirm your eligibility for the scheme. Please ensure you obtain one during the application process, through UK ENIC: https://www.enic.org.uk/
- Previous qualifications will be reviewed for funding eligibility and offers are subject to funding approval
- PLEASE NOTE: This position is a 48 month fixed-term contract. You must NOT already have a qualification in a similar subject at the same or higher level than this apprenticeship.
- This Apprenticeship assumes the candidate has some or little knowledge/experience of the occupation

Preferred qualifications

- An interest in operations, logistics, or supply chain environments
- A genuine enthusiasm for leading, motivating, and working with people
- Natural leadership instincts - the kind of person who steps up without being asked
- Resilient and able to prioritise under pressure - staying composed when the pace is demanding and there’s a lot to juggle
- Great communication skills and naturally able to influence others
- A problem-solving mindset and a willingness to learn
- Comfortable with change and able to stay calm in a fast-paced environment
- Happy working in fast-paced warehouse environment, including shift work (days, nights, and weekends)

descriptionHtml:
AWS Global Deal Strategy and Programs (GDSP) is responsible for the strategy, structure, and execution of AWS's largest customer deals worldwide. The organization operates at the intersection of pricing economics, deal execution, and customer relationships across all AWS segments and geographies.

GDSP is seeking a Senior Product Manager - Technical to own the product vision and strategy for the analytical and automation products that operationalize deal workflows, automate reporting, and surface insights to deal teams globally. These products serve deal strategists, pricing leaders, and senior executives who depend on them daily to structure, evaluate, and negotiate transformative contracts with the most strategic AWS customers.

An ideal candidate pinpoints answers from broad data sets (deal telemetry, pricing models, customer usage, pipeline signals) at unprecedented scale, with speed and accuracy that does scales with volume growth. The role requires deep analytical acumen, the ability to define what questions matter most, and the product judgment to deliver answers in forms that drive action without sacrificing rigor.

This is a high-visibility role. Outputs are consumed directly by GDSP leadership and AWS executives. Product decisions in this space have immediate, measurable impact on deal velocity, pricing quality, and revenue outcomes.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the 3 to 5 year product vision and roadmap for deal intelligence and automation capabilities across GDSP
- Define products that leverage broad data sets (deal telemetry, pricing history, customer usage patterns, pipeline signals) to deliver precise, actionable insights at global scale
- Partner with engineering to evaluate architectural trade-offs, including where AI, automation, and agentic systems create the highest analytical and operational leverage
- Establish mechanisms (metrics frameworks, operational cadences, experimentation strategies) that make delivery repeatable and raise the quality bar across the organization
- Influence and align stakeholders across multiple organizations to remove obstacles and deliver outcomes
- Engage directly with customers (deal strategists, pricing leaders, GDSP executives) to validate direction and ensure the platform evolves ahead of demand
- Create product artifacts (PR/FAQs, strategy narratives, business cases) that build alignment with senior leadership

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
- Experience managing technical products or online services
- Experience in representing and advocating for a variety of critical customers and stakeholders during executive-level prioritization and planning

title: RME Mechatronics Apprentice – South Wales (36-month fixed term contract)
descriptionHtml:
Fascinated by the mechanics behind automated systems? Want to master both electrical and mechanical engineering while working with cutting-edge technology? Amazon is the perfect place to launch your career in Mechatronics Maintenance.

As one of the world's most advanced technology-driven companies, we're powered by automation, robotics, and continuous innovation - from robotic arms to complex conveyor networks and smart sensor technology that keep millions of customer orders moving. This apprenticeship gives you the chance to become a multi-skilled maintenance technician across both electrical and mechanical disciplines, with hands-on experience on industry-leading equipment, some of which only exists at Amazon.

Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team is fundamental to our operations - they keep vital machinery running around the clock. As an RME Mechatronics Apprentice, you'll help maintain a wide range of equipment while upholding Health and Safety best practice, keeping your colleagues safe, preventing downtime, and improving the availability and quality of our equipment.

You'll thrive here if you stay calm when things go wrong and get a real kick out of fixing them. You're hands-on, curious about how machines work, and you understand that keeping production moving is what it's all about. And you don't need to be a qualified engineer to start - what matters most is a practical, problem-solving mindset and a hunger to learn.

A day in the life can involve:

- Carrying out proactive and preventative maintenance
- Carrying out reactive repairs and fault diagnosis in a live distribution warehouse
- Using the latest tools to maximise equipment effectiveness
- Making modifications and upgrades to existing equipment
- Upholding health and safety policies and practices
- Working on continuous improvement projects, and suggesting long-term improvements

Throughout your apprenticeship, you'll build a broad, in-demand engineering skillset, including:

- Fault diagnosis and preventative maintenance
- Mechanical device maintenance, and fluid power systems assembly and testing
- Electrical equipment wiring and testing
- Hydraulics and pneumatics
- Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) operations
- CAD design and 3D printing

Here at Amazon, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Within this apprenticeship, you'll learn by doing, putting newfound knowledge into practice every day. Our first-class coaching, tailored development opportunities, and challenging, rewarding work will empower you to reach new heights. If you're a curious learner eager to grow, this is your chance to unlock your full potential and build the future you envision.

Throughout the apprenticeship you'll work towards an Advanced Apprenticeship in Engineering (Mechatronics Maintenance), combining practical, on-the-job experience with industry-recognised study. Your first 12 months will be a full-time residential programme, based either at one of our external training provider facilities or at our own world-class Amazon training centres - reflecting our significant investment in developing state-of-the-art facilities for the next generation of engineers. If you live outside a commutable distance, accommodation will be provided during term time for these first 12 months, and travel expenses will be supported.

Please note: some of our training sites aren't accessible by public transport, so you'll need to be able to arrange reliable travel to and from site. Access to a car can make this easier but isn't essential.

In later years, you'll combine day or block-release study for your qualification in Engineering or Mechatronics with on-the-job training at one of our Fulfilment Centres, Sortation Centres, or Delivery Stations, learning directly from experienced technicians and engineers and gaining exposure to real engineering projects.

This role supports our 24/7 operation, so you'll work shifts covering days, nights and weekends - patterns that reflect the real-world schedules of the engineers who keep Amazon operating around the clock.

This apprenticeship trains you for a variety of maintenance roles - mechatronic maintenance technician, maintenance engineer, mechanical fitter, and electrical engineer - with plenty of opportunities for progression both within RME and more widely across Amazon. This could be the start of an exciting and rewarding career.

You'll join a diverse and passionate team of engineers dedicated to driving results and pushing creative boundaries. We value different perspectives and experiences, and we're dedicated to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. Our employee-led affinity groups - including communities for women in tech, LGBTQ+ employees, and underrepresented minorities - foster a culture of inclusion that empowers us to be proud of our differences. These groups provide community, mentorship, and a platform for your voice to be heard. We're committed to building a workforce that reflects the customers and communities we serve.

We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a well-rounded professional.

Join us and be part of the team that keeps Amazon moving. Apply now and shape the future of technology with us.

As part of the recruitment and enrolment process for this apprenticeship, candidates must provide proof of all required qualifications. Original certificates or certified copies must be submitted - this is a mandatory requirement to secure the position. The deadline for providing qualification certificates for the RME Mechatronics programme is 16 July 2027. Applications without verified qualifications by this date will automatically be unsuccessful, and failure to provide proof by the deadline will result in the withdrawal of any conditional offer, meaning you will not be able to commence the programme. - Have lived in the UK or in the European Economic Area (EEA) for the last 3 years prior to the start date
- Not be registered to study on a UK government funded course ending August 2027 or later

title: Maintenance Engineering Planner, Reliability Maintenance Engineering
descriptionHtml:
We are looking for motivated, customer-focused people who want to join our team as a Reliability Maintenance Engineering Planner. The Reliability Maintenance Engineering Planner is responsible for asset and spares management, preventative maintenance planning and machine history data. They are the site lead for the CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) software and are required to extract information from it to support the site engineering manager.

Key job responsibilities
- Be the site level SME (Subject Matter Expert) on the CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) software, train the local engineering team in its use and escalate issues as required to the Global team.
- Ensure the system is run in line with IntlRME standards and participate in IntlRME coordinated projects and improvement programs to roll out new functionality, procedures, scheduling or reports.
- Ensure site level equipment, spare parts and minimum holding levels are correctly recorded in the system in order to ensure technicians are never without the parts they need.
- Ensure the system accurately forecasts and assigns all required preventative maintenance to technicians within the team to provide a high level of equipment availability to our internal customers.
- Compile equipment information, performance metrics and machine histories and make recommendations for improvements based on their findings.
- Manage spare parts stock levels, place and track orders as required. Work with procurement and the wider BR network to find savings or efficiencies.

About the team
Amazon Operations sits at the heart of the Amazon customer experience. We look after everything from the moment a customer clicks buy, to the moment their item is delivered – from desktop to doorstep.

Across Mexico we have several Fulfillment Centers, Sort Center and Delivery Stations, thousands of machines, and thousands of employees, all working together in harmony to make sure the right item gets delivered to the right person, in the right place, at the right time.

Working in Amazon Operations is for people who like to be active and give their all. We work in a busy, dynamic environment and are part of a bigger team delivering on the expectations of millions of customers every single day.

We are open, inclusive and welcome individuality and diversity. The culture in our Operation is built on the way teams bond and the work ethic that enables our business run like clockwork. Our teams take pride in a job well done, looking out for one another, ensuring the highest safety standards and playing their part in delivering the quality service Amazon is known for around the world.

Join us in the Amazon Reliability Maintenance Engineering team. We maintain and optimize technologies in the Global Amazon Warehouse & Delivery Network.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 2+ years of maintenance or engineering experience, or experience in reliability/maintenance environments
- 1+ years of Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) experience
- Experience in computer skills, including proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
- Experience in oral and written communication in English

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of maintenance planner/scheduler in industrial maintenance, manufacturing, or distribution industries experience
- Experience working with CMMS software, or experience in reliability/maintenance environments
- Experience in operations or inventory management
- Experience in creating process improvements with automation and analysis, or experience applying key financial performance indicators (KPIs) to analyses
- Experience in project management, or experience in vendor management
- Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or 1+ years of conducting predictive and preventative maintenance procedures experience

Many of the world's fastest growing businesses, such as Lyft, Airbnb, and Redfin, as well as enterprises, such as Samsung, Toyota, and Capital One, depend on the scale and performance of DynamoDB to support their mission-critical workloads.

title: Mechatronics & Robotics Tech
descriptionHtml:
About Maintenance at Amazon

Operations is at the heart of Amazon’s business. We are known for our speed, accuracy, and exceptional service. Our buildings deliver tens of thousands of products to hundreds of countries worldwide, every day. Reliability Maintenance & Engineering (RME) are the business partners that work tirelessly behind the scenes to make it all happen. We drive continuous improvement and maintain all of the Robotics and Material Handling Equipment (MHE) to ensure our customers are met with the Amazon smile. Come join us on our journey!

About the Role

As a Mechatronics & Robotics Technician, you will use your skills to support the Operations Maintenance team in repairing and maintaining material handling equipment and pneumatic systems throughout the building. You will have the opportunity to install, maintain, and repair automated packaging and distribution equipment. In addition to developing your skills, you will mentor junior technicians to grow in their roles.

What Do We Offer?

Amazon offers competitive compensation packages including comprehensive healthcare benefits starting on Day 1, matching 401(k) program, and up to 20 weeks of paid parental leave. But wait, there is more: We provide lightweight fire-resistant daily wear and composite toe safety shoes for your safety!

Here is what you can expect with the Reliability & Maintenance Engineering (RME) selection process for Mechatronics & Robotics Technicians: (Timeframe: Approximately 30-days)

Step 1: Congratulations! You successfully submitted your application!

Step 2: Amazon Recruiting will review your application and invite the most qualified candidate to complete a pre-employment assessment.

Step 3: If you meet the role qualifications, you will receive an invitation from Amazon Recruiting (do-not-reply@criteriacorp.com) to begin your Criteria assessment. You have 5 days to complete.

Step 4: Once you successfully meet the pre-employment assessment requirements, you will be invited to complete a video interview. Your video interview invitation will be from HireVue (interviews@hirevue.com) and you will have 7 days to record your interview.

Step 5: Your video interview will be reviewed by the Amazon Hiring Team and you will be notified of next steps via email within 5 business days.


Key job responsibilities
Key job responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
- You will promote a safe working environment by following all safety procedures
- You will complete preventative maintenance routines with proper documentation
- You will troubleshoot electrical and mechanical problems related to all Material Handling Equipment (MHE) which includes belts, motors, photo-eyes, relays, and more
- You will maintain a positive working relationship across all of the Amazon Operations facility
- You must be able to move up to 49lbs, stand and walk during shifts lasting up to 12 hours, climb ladders and gangways safely, and without limitation, as well as perform regular bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching both below the waist and above the head

title: Pre-Construction Manager, GES NA, Design and Construction
descriptionHtml:
As a Preconstruction Manager within Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Design & Construction (D&C), you are Amazon's owner's representative during the preconstruction phase — responsible for independently managing difficult, cross-functional industrial building projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution across your assigned region. Preconstruction services refers to the planning of a construction project before actual construction begins.

You will partner with internal and external stakeholders to ensure scope, budget, and schedule definition are established, including timely receipt of building and site permits. You are responsible as the project manager to lead planning, design, and preconstruction projects — including new built-to-suit industrial buildings, tenant improvements, extensions of existing facilities, and renovation projects — supporting Amazon's logistics network infrastructure.

You work independently within your assigned region, using your knowledge of construction and project management concepts to decide which actions to take to complete projects, and seeking guidance as needed on strategic components. You are tactical with some strategic components, utilizing well-defined processes and best practices to facilitate delivery of high-quality results. You make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources to keep projects on track.

Key competencies of this position include ensuring that contracted resources deliver work product in support of project durations, permitting, key performance indicators (KPIs), and quality documentation; managing project teams (developers, design engineers, professional consultants); influencing internal teams (Design Engineering, Amazon Robotics); contract management governance; conceptual estimating and budget oversight; and managing multiple large industrial projects in various locations simultaneously. Translating technical documents and information into clear, concise narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers is essential.

This opportunity combines construction engineering, planning, project management, real estate development, design validation, site visits, understanding of local building and fire code issues, utilities, sustainability, multi-disciplinary design management, and contract management. The Preconstruction Manager is responsible for the planning and design of scope, budget, and schedule prior to handing off to the Construction Manager — focusing on taking ownership to resolve upstream issues and supporting the construction team throughout the process.

This role requires approximately 60% regional travel within North America, with potential travel to all North America locations based on business needs.

Key job responsibilities
Safety & Compliance
- Supervise the implementation and management of Amazon's safety programs and standards across all internal and external project teams during the planning and preconstruction phases of a project
- Interface and coordinate with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to ensure regulatory compliance, smooth permitting execution, and timely approvals
- Review noise, traffic, and environmental studies; understand zoning, planning, fire code, and building code requirements for assigned projects

Preconstruction & Project Management
- Independently manage difficult, cross-functional industrial preconstruction projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution
- Lead site selection and validation, scope development, and design management — coordinating with design teams to develop site plans and composite floor plans in compliance with Amazon's design standards and operational requirements
- Manage multiple concurrent large industrial projects across various locations simultaneously
- Keep scope under control and accelerate progress by driving crisp, timely decisions, identifying and clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately
- Identify and resolve upstream issues proactively to support a clean handoff to the Construction Manager; remain a key support resource for the construction team throughout the project lifecycle
- Assess project performance through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and sustainability
- Minimize disruptions and proactively mitigate risks; plan ahead to prevent problems before they happen

Budget, Schedule & Contract Management
- Develop and manage project budgets and costs; own comprehensive schedule management and cashflow forecasting across assigned preconstruction projects
- Perform conceptual estimating and pricing reviews for scope inclusions and exclusions; negotiate the cost of work with developers, general contractors, and design consultants
- Contribute to the selection of external vendor partners and manage vendor procurement; oversee professional service providers to ensure their skills and competencies meet project requirements
- Review and analyze design and construction contracts, related exhibits, and lease agreements; provide detailed analysis of technical matters and site-specific deal structures and terms
- Partner with the Transaction team and developers to optimize schedule and strategy for entitlements and long-lead procurement
- Identify and solve factors that may impede a successful permitted project handover to Amazon stakeholders; make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
- Work with internal and external teams — including Real Estate, Design Engineering, Entitlements, Construction, Finance, Launch/Startup, architects, engineers, permitting agencies, developers, and landlords — to secure resources, scope infrastructure builds, set priorities and milestones, and drive delivery to meet deadlines
- Drive results through communicating, weighing risks, making decisions, leading, and influencing; competently represent project and technical information to diverse audiences
- Maintain good working relationships with stakeholders and vendors; lead constructive dialogue to resolve and prevent project issues
- Act as the primary escalation point for project team members; own and track issues to ensure they are addressed, documented, and resolved

Communication & Reporting
- Prepare and present project status and risk reports; provide clear, concise summaries for projects under your ownership to leadership and management teams
- Translate technical documents and information into end-to-end narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers
- Run preconstruction meetings effectively — putting the right people in the room, checking progress, and driving high-level alignment and consensus
- Communicate budgets, schedules, project status, and priorities clearly to internal teams and external partners; trusted to present decisions to leaders up to 2-3 tiers above level
- Utilize Amazon's information systems to record and update schedule, budget, and other key project developments
- Represent Amazon's interests in weekly Architect, Owner, and Contractor (AOC) meetings; provide input on root causes and corrective actions

Process Improvement & Innovation
- Optimize preconstruction processes and implement improvements in procedures and playbooks to improve project efficiency and delivery
- Look for opportunities to improve operational excellence and influence the team to determine where to iterate and make improvements
- Seek sustainable, environmentally responsible solutions throughout the preconstruction process in alignment with Amazon's building practices
- Adapt to constant change and innovation; find adaptable solutions for an evolving business

A day in the life
Each day, you represent GES NA Design & Construction as Amazon's owner during the preconstruction phase — navigating uncertainty, proactively unblocking project barriers, and influencing the best project decisions. title: Sr Manufacturing NPI Product Engineer, AWS Mainstream Compute
descriptionHtml:
AWS operates the world's largest fleet of general compute servers at cloud scale. Our team takes these platforms from design into high-volume production, owning the manufacturing processes, test strategies, and quality systems that determine whether a new server ships on time and at the right quality. If you want to own how the hardware that frontier models train on actually gets built, this is the role.

We are seeking a Sr Manufacturing Product Engineer to drive New Product Introduction (NPI) manufacturing and quality for volume compute server platforms, from early design engagement through volume production. You will define manufacturing processes, test flows, and quality controls, serve as the primary manufacturing engineering interface between hardware design, supply chain, and ODM partners, and ensure products are optimized for manufacturability and launched at exceptional quality.

What You Will Do

You will own how a new compute platform is manufactured. You will engage with hardware design early to influence testability and manufacturability, define the manufacturing test strategy and quality plan, and drive the process from prototype through Pilot and volume ramp. You will run NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments before design freeze, lead design reviews, and drive root cause corrective action on manufacturing blockers and quality escapes. When a platform ramps to volume with high first-pass yield and no quality escapes reaching the fleet, that is your impact.

Why You Will Love It

Millions of organizations run diverse workloads on the AWS compute hardware you help build. You will see your process and test decisions scale across a large fleet of servers, and you will work at the point where design meets the factory floor. The team is deeply technical and high-trust, and you own manufacturing outcomes end to end from design engagement through volume production.

The Ideal Candidate

You think across the full manufacturing stack, from SMT assembly and test coverage to line balance, yield, and quality systems. You are as comfortable in a DFx review reading gerber files as you are on an ODM floor debugging a failing test station. You drive decisions with data, hold manufacturing partners to a high bar, and bring structured problem-solving and disciplined change management to a fast-moving NPI environment. You mentor junior engineers, contribute to hiring, and raise the manufacturing engineering bar for the team.



Key job responsibilities
Design for Manufacturability & Risk
- Perform NUDD (New, Unique, Difficult, Different) risk assessments and carry-over analysis to identify and mitigate manufacturing risks before design freeze
- Participate in DFx reviews (DFM/DFA/DFT) leveraging mechanical CAD models, gerber files, and mock-up samples, driving design improvements in partnership with hardware engineering
- Lead DFMEA/PFMEA reviews and develop process flow diagrams and quality control plans
NPI Manufacturing & Test Strategy
- Own end-to-end NPI manufacturing execution for volume compute platforms across engineering phases and Pilot builds
- Define the manufacturing test strategy including test flows, coverage, duration, fixture requirements such as in circuit tests (ICT), board functional test (BFT) and system-level tests.
- Own Contract Manufacturer enablement including BOM requirements, assembly workflows, testing protocols, and tooling specifications
- Research automation techniques and develop new tests and systems to improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce test dwell time
Quality & Continuous Improvement
- Drive Root Cause Corrective Action (RCCA) for manufacturing blockers and quality escapes
- Execute test rack inspections and quality checklists; issue quality alerts, deviations, and ship-holds as required
- Own manufacturing quality metrics and drive yield improvement, and cost optimization through process and automation engineering
Capacity & Production Ramp
- Create manufacturing capacity plans with simulations across build phases; conduct line balance and cycle time analysis to maximize throughput
- Provide on-site ODM support during critical builds and production ramp
- Collaborate with suppliers and internal teams on system integration, thermal validation, and manufacturing requirements


Cross-Team Collaboration
- Serve as the primary manufacturing engineering interface between hardware design, supply chain, and ODM/CM partners
- Manage manufacturing requirements, scope, schedules, and deliverables across engineering teams, suppliers, and partners
- Perform risk assessment, mitigation, and change management throughout the program lifecycle
Domestic and international travel (~25%) to ODM/CM and design partner sites.


A day in the life
You start the day reviewing first-pass yield data from an overnight Pilot build at your ODM, isolating a test station driving a recurring failure. Mid-morning, you lead a DFx review with hardware design, pushing changes to improve testability before design freeze. In the afternoon, you drive an RCCA on a solder defect with the CM quality team and update the control plan. You end the day refining the capacity plan and line balance for the next build phase.

About the team
The Hardware Engineering Mainstream Compute platform team is a group of engineers and technical program managers directly responsible for launching high volume computer servers into the AWS fleet. Located in Seattle, Austin, and Cupertino, we collaborate with global development teams and ODM/CM partners to deliver next-generation server infrastructure deployed in datacenters worldwide. We move fast with small, empowered teams delivering end-to-end, from server conception through volume production and fleet-scale operations.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing Engineering or similar related field or equivalent experience.
- 5+ years of high volume manufacturing experience in server, automotive, or aerospace industries, spanning NPI, process development or production engineering.
- 3+ years of end-to-end NPI product delivery experience from concept through volume production
- Strong data analysis skills using statistical tools (JMP, Minitab, Excel, Python) to drive data-driven decisions
- Experience driving quality and schedule execution at multinational JDM, ODM, CM, and supplier partners

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing and coordinating multiple projects simultaneously
- Master's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field
- Experience working with interdisciplinary teams to execute product design in manufacturing from concept to volume production.
- Knowledge of Six Sigma, Lean Manufacturing, SPC, FMEA, PFMEA, or Root Cause Analysis.
- Experience conducting DFM/DFX reviews and risk assessments for complex hardware systems.
- Experience evaluating and qualifying new design partners or manufacturing locations.
- Experience with NUDD analysis and manufacturing risk assessment methodologies.
- Experience assessing and qualifying new manufacturing technologies for volume production readiness.
- Experience with DOE (Design of Experiments), MSA (Measurement System Analysis), GR&R studies, and process capability analysis in a production setting
- Track record of driving shift-left manufacturing initiatives that reduced NPI cycle time or improved first-pass yield

title: Supply Chain Analyst, GPCS - AMER
descriptionHtml:
The Supply Chain Analyst is responsible for building and maintaining the reporting infrastructure that enables data-driven decision making across GPCS. This includes owning KPI dashboards, supplier and inventory visibility tools, launch tracking, pricing analysis, and deep-dive reporting that surfaces defects and operational gaps at the site and supplier level.

The Supply Chain Analyst is the owner of GPCS operational reporting accuracy — monitoring the quality and consistency of data across reporting surfaces, and partnering with system owners (including Coupa, Delphi, and other source systems) to drive resolution when data is incorrect or inconsistent.
This role requires proficiency in dashboard development (e.g., QuickSight, Asana, or equivalent BI tools), SQL or equivalent query languages, and the ability to translate complex operational data into clear, actionable reports for stakeholder groups that include finance, operations, ACES, and internal GPO teams.

Successful candidates are natural self-starters who thrive in ambiguous, fast-changing environments. This role requires someone who is highly adaptable — capable of quickly adjusting strategies and implementation plans in response to dynamic business needs and varying site conditions. The ideal candidate excels at managing multiple stakeholder relationships, driving consistent standards across diverse partners, and balancing technical requirements with operational constraints.

Key job responsibilities
Dashboard and Reporting Infrastructure
Build, maintain, and report on KPI dashboards that serve as the single source of truth for GPCS operational performance
Develop and manage supplier ETA and inventory level dashboards at the site and vendor level
Maintain the SEV2 Asana dashboard and produce miss reports that surface root causes and prevention recommendations to reduce SEV2 reoccurrence, distributed to stakeholder groups including operations and internal GPO teams

Ad Hoc and On-Demand Reporting
Produce cross-team project status reporting on a defined cadence
Conduct pricing change reporting and build ad hoc reports or dashboards as requested by stakeholders to address emerging business questions, one-time analytical needs, or leadership requests outside the standard reporting cadence
Support ad hoc data collection, reporting and dashboard creation across supply and inventory topics — such as excess inventory exposure, forecast versus orders performance, supplier stock shortage risks, cycle count values versus usage, and invoice hold trends.

Analysis and Deep Dives
Perform deep-dive analyses on recurring operational issues and escalations, including ordering logic failures, system trigger anomalies, and stakeholder-submitted questions

Data Accuracy and Governance
Conduct regular audits of dashboard data against source-of-truth systems; document discrepancies, corrective actions, and recurring failure patterns — and escalate pipeline-level issues to the AI/Automation Specialist for technical resolution
Establish and maintain data definitions, metric formulas, and refresh cadences that are consistent across all GPCS dashboards and business reviews

About the team
Global Procurement Central Services (GPCS) is a centralized corporate team that provides non-inventory procurement support across Amazon's operational network. GPCS manages the end-to-end supply chain of forecasting, purchasing, delivery, escalation management, and financial reconciliation. This role within GPCS will support the operational readiness of Amazon's emerging and growing business lines, including programs such as Prime Air, ensuring sites have the non-inventory supplies and consumables needed to operate effectively. This is a critical role in building scalable procurement processes that support network growth and expansion.

Basic qualifications

- Experience in Finance, Supply Chain Management, Business, IT or any other procurement related career
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent, or 1+ years of Amazon experience
- 2+ years of business analytics and reporting or demand forecasting experience
- Experience in data analysis and reporting
- Knowledge of supply chain management concepts - forecasting, planning, sourcing, optimization and logistics or equivalent
- Experience in Excel with advanced proficiency (pivots, lookups, etc.)
- Experience managing multiple projects and priorities across teams in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of SQL at an intermediate level, including: compile queries, subqueries, aggregation/grouping, data modification, etc.
- Knowledge of data visualization tools such as Quick Sight, Tableau, Power BI or other BI packages
- Experience in technical support, or experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities and experience working with customers with a passion for delivering exceptional service
- 3+ months of project coordination experience

title: Security Engineer III, Customer Service Security
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to protect customers at a global scale while seeing the direct impact of your work? The Customer Service Security team at Amazon is looking for a Systems Security Engineer who thrives in ambiguity and is passionate about engineering solutions that reduce security risk across customer service operations. With billions of customer contacts per year spanning more than 40 countries, the security challenges here are complex and the stakes are real.

In this role, you will partner directly with business teams to identify security risks, design pragmatic controls, and build solutions that simultaneously improve security outcomes, customer experiences, and associate experiences. You will own security architecture decisions, lead risk mitigation discussions, and construct frameworks that enable others to apply your work in a repeatable way. If you are a self-starter who can navigate undefined problems and turn them into scalable security solutions, we want to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead security reviews, threat modeling, and risk assessments for customer service systems, identifying pragmatic approaches to mitigate risks while enabling teams to launch securely.
- Design and build security controls and engineering solutions that protect customer data and empower secure customer contacts at scale.
- Partner with business stakeholders, product owners, and engineering teams to understand emerging risks and define security strategies where none yet exist.
- Create security frameworks, runbooks, and rubrics for new problem domains that enable other engineers to apply consistent, repeatable security practices.

descriptionHtml:

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. • Helping to train and onboard new team members

Physical requirements:
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 40 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 41+ pounds
• Working in cramped and/or elevated locations
• Bending, lifting, stretching, and reaching
• Standing and walking for up to 8+ hours a day
• Ascending and descending ladders, stairs, and gangways safely and without limitation
• Work in a noisy environment
• Work shifts longer than 8 hours to support 24/7 operations (covering both night and day shifts).
This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
• Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
• Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.

You will be required to work shift work that will include days/nights/weekends/holidays. Traveling within and outside of the regional work area is required. You will be responsible for having a reliable personal vehicle and valid driver's license to travel within the regional work area, as company transportation will not be provided.

title: Supply Planning Manager, Amazon Robotics, Tech Supply Chain - Technology Materials Planning
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's technology supply chain supports a complex and rapidly evolving portfolio of infrastructure, end-user equipment, and technology products across thousands of locations globally. As the business scales, disciplined and responsive supply planning is critical to ensuring material availability, managing inventory investment, optimizing procurement execution, enabling network efficiency, and delivering predictable outcomes for customers.

We are seeking a Manager, Supply Planning to lead the supply planning capability within Supply Chain Planning. This leader will manage a team responsible for developing and continuously improving supply plans across the existing customer business segments, while establishing scalable mechanisms that can support new businesses, products, and fulfillment models.

The successful candidate will build a supply planning organization that combines strong planning fundamentals with data, technology, and automation. This includes improving material requirement plan quality, integrating demand signals with supply constraints and lead times, optimizing network topology through hub-and-spoke and regional distribution strategies, identifying structural sources of supply risk and excess inventory, and partnering with Product, Data, Analytics, and Technology teams to reduce manual planning activity and enable increasingly intelligent supply planning capabilities.

The ideal candidate combines strong supply chain expertise, analytical depth, customer orientation, business judgment, and people leadership. They must be comfortable challenging assumptions, navigating incomplete or conflicting signals, and influencing stakeholders across Supply Chain, Finance, Technology, Operations, Procurement, and customer organizations.

Key job responsibilities
- Lead, coach, and develop a team responsible for supply planning across Launch, KTLO, and Programs.
- Own the end-to-end supply planning mechanism, including material requirement plan (MRP) creation and execution, order management, inventory performance measurement, and continuous improvement.
- Translate demand plans, supply constraints, lead times, funding availability, and inventory positions into executable material requirement plans at the appropriate product, geographic, and time horizons.
- Establish clear accountability for supply inputs and challenge assumptions, overrides, and changes that are not supported by measurable business signals or supply data.
- Define and improve supply availability, inventory health, Days of Cover, excess and obsolescence, order accuracy, and other metrics that distinguish true supply variability from process, data, and system defects.
- Lead capacity planning efforts to ensure supplier and network capacity aligns with demand forecasts, proactively identifying and mitigating capacity constraints across the planning horizon.
- Design and optimize hub-and-spoke distribution and network topology strategies to improve fulfillment speed, reduce transportation costs, and support regional inventory positioning across global sites.
- Partner with Demand Planning and Enterprise S&OP to incorporate demand uncertainty, quantify supply risks, and support scenario and trade-off decisions.
- Develop segmented planning approaches appropriate for different supply patterns, including new site launches, steady-state replenishment, and program-driven procurement, incorporating network optimization principles to determine optimal stocking locations and replenishment flows.
- Partner with Product, Data, Analytics, and Technology teams to automate material requirement plan generation, order validation, exception management, and planner workflows.
- Advance the use of optimization models, machine learning, and AI to improve supply plan quality and reduce dependence on manual reconciliation and judgment.
- Simplify fragmented supply processes and data sources, with a long-term goal of connecting Planning more directly to real-time inventory positions, supplier capacity, network capacity utilization, and procurement execution.
- Build scalable mechanisms that support new products, businesses, regions, and planning paradigms without creating parallel planning processes.
- Communicate supply outlook, inventory risks, capacity constraints, network optimization opportunities, funding gaps, procurement constraints, and recommended actions clearly to senior stakeholders.
- Travel 20% of the time to Fulfillment Centers across Europe


A day in the life
In this role, you may begin the day reviewing inventory positions and open order status with your team, determining whether a supply gap reflects a true constraint or a defect in the underlying data or process. You may evaluate hub capacity utilization and assess whether regional inventory positioning is aligned with current demand patterns.

You may work with Demand Planning to understand the implications of a forecast change on the material requirement plan, partner with Procurement to resolve a supplier lead time or capacity issue, or support Enterprise S&OP with scenarios where supply constraints, network bottlenecks, or funding gaps require a broader business decision.

You may also spend time with Product or Technology teams improving how material requirement plans are generated, automating a repetitive planner workflow, optimizing network flows across hub-and-spoke distribution points, or defining how optimization models and AI can augment planner judgment.

The role balances near-term supply performance with the longer-term objective of creating a scalable, technology-enabled supply planning capability where planners spend less time collecting and reconciling information and more time managing supply risk, optimizing network and inventory investment, and improving the quality of the plan.

- Experience setting team goals and roadmaps, capacity planning, lead times, cost and quality, and owning complex, multi-team programs, through to measurable business results
- Experience influencing cross-functional stakeholders and senior leaders, and presenting business documents to leadership
- Experience with data analysis tools such as SQL, advanced Excel, Python and Tableau or QuickSight to define and track metrics (KPIs, SLAs) and drive decisions
